claim.pdf_says: Format 2 (historic):   IF condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / NEXT SENTENCE } [ ELSE { statement-2 / NEXT SENTENCE } ]   — with IF, NEXT, SENTENCE (both occurrences) and ELSE UNDERLINED; THEN, statement-1, statement-2 NOT underlined.
claim.markdown_says: IF condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / NEXT SENTENCE } [ ELSE { statement-2 / NEXT SENTENCE } ]   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27469 — no <u> markup on any word)
claim.why_it_matters: Same required-word loss as Format 1, and here it also erases that NEXT and SENTENCE are each individually underlined (both are required words of the NEXT SENTENCE phrase). The brace/bracket structure and the ASCII '/' rendering of the stacked alternatives are faithful; only the underlining is lost.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed by rendering spec_p665.png at 300 dpi (printed page 635, clause 14.9.19.2) and re-reading the Format 2 figure at 2x and 4x magnification. Glyphs actually printed, read directly: 'IF' carries a short horizontal rule beneath it (underlined); 'condition-1' has no rule; 'THEN' has NO rule (verified at 4x — there is unambiguously no underline under THEN); 'statement-1' no rule; 'NEXT' carries its own rule and 'SENTENCE' carries a second, visibly separate rule with a clear gap between them; 'ELSE' is underlined; 'statement-2' has no rule; the second 'NEXT' and second 'SENTENCE' are again each separately underlined. The claim's description of the PDF is accurate in every particular. The markdown Format 2 line carries no underline markup of any kind. ADVERSARIAL CHECKS ALL FAIL TO REFUTE: (1) The information is not merely reflowed or on an adjacent line — a scan of specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 27400-27600 finds no <u> markup and no 'Figure notes' annotation attached to either IF format (the only 'Figure notes' block in that window, at line 27573, belongs to 5.2.6.4 choice indicators, a different page region). The page-665 workunit likewise reported '0 with figure content', corroborating that the figure was flattened to plain text. (2) It is not formatting-only furniture. ISO/IEC 1989:2023 5.2.2 (Keywords): 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword'; 5.2.3 (Optional words): 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity.' Underlining is therefore the SOLE normative carrier of required-word versus optional-word status in a general format, so its loss is a loss of normative content, not of styling. (3) The transcription's own conventions confirm this: it preserves underlining elsewhere via 97 <u> occurrences and via many explicit 'Figure notes (...) are underlined in the printed standard (required words)' blocks — so page 665 is a genuine omission against the document's own standard, not a global stylistic policy. (4) The markdown is quoted exactly. (5) Meaning does change: from the markdown alone an implementer cannot tell that THEN is an optional word (omissible — 'IF X = 1 NEXT SENTENCE' is legal) while IF, ELSE, NEXT and SENTENCE are keywords that must be written. The brace/bracket structure and the '/' rendering of the stacked alternatives are, as the claim concedes, faithful. Only the claim's citation detail and one emphasis are off, corrected below.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, with two corrections to the claim's framing. (a) Line number: the Format 2 line is specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27472, not 27469 (27469 is a blank line; 27468 is the Format 1 line, 27470 is 'Format 2 (historic):'). (b) Emphasis: the normatively load-bearing loss is the keyword/optional-word distinction mandated by 5.2.2 and 5.2.3 — that IF, ELSE, NEXT and SENTENCE are keywords (required) while THEN is an optional word (may be omitted). The claim's added stress on NEXT and SENTENCE being *individually* underlined rather than sharing one continuous rule is cosmetically accurate (the printed page does show two separate rules with a visible gap, in both occurrences) but carries no distinct normative weight: either rendering yields the same reading that both words are required. Accurate statement of the defect: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27472 transcribes the clause 14.9.19.2 Format 2 general format as plain ASCII with no <u> markup and no compensating figure-notes annotation, dropping the underlines the printed standard sets under IF, ELSE, and both occurrences of NEXT and of SENTENCE, and thereby erasing the only signal that THEN — printed without an underline — is an optional word. The identical loss affects the Format 1 line at 27468 (IF, ELSE, END-IF underlined in print; THEN not). Suggested fix: mark up as 'IF condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / NEXT SENTENCE } [ ELSE { statement-2 / NEXT SENTENCE } ]' with <u> on IF, ELSE, and each NEXT and SENTENCE, or add a 'Figure notes' block naming the underlined words, matching the convention already used elsewhere in the transcription.
